expected_title: VNF and CNF Placement in 5G: Recent Advances and Future Trends
summary: Survey that builds a taxonomy of optimisation techniques for placing virtualised and containerised network functions in 5G, extending the classic VNF placement problem to CNFs in edge/fog settings.
method: Systematic survey and taxonomy (metrics, methods, algorithms, environment)
key_result: Organises VNF/CNF placement literature by objective (latency, congestion, utilisation, energy) and solution class (exact, heuristic, ML), and lists open problems for cloud-native 5G.
limitation_or_critique: Treats placement generically for VNFs/CNFs and does not specifically model 5GC control-plane semantics such as NRF/SCP-mediated NF selection.

expected_title: Cloud-Native Service Mesh Readiness for 5G and Beyond
summary: Review-style analysis of how service meshes can realise the 3GPP SBA in cloud-native deployments, covering service-to-service communication, discovery and programmability for 5G core signalling.
method: Qualitative review and architectural design (Envoy extension for 5G SBI semantics)
key_result: Argues that off-the-shelf meshes lack 5G-specific semantics and proposes Envoy-based enhancements that map SCP-like indirect communication onto a service mesh.
limitation_or_critique: Largely conceptual with no quantitative evaluation of the proposed mesh enhancements or of AI-driven routing/selection policies.

expected_title: Prospects on the adoption of a microservice-based architecture in 5G systems and beyond
summary: Position/review paper arguing that the 5GC needs deeper re-design into true microservices and illustrating the decomposition of three example network functions into services with distinct responsibilities.
method: Architectural analysis and NF decomposition (theoretical and practical)
data_or_testbed: Prototype decomposition of example NFs (industrial partners, PREDICT-6G)
key_result: Shows that 3GPP NFs as specified remain coarse-grained and proposes a decomposition approach and directions for beyond-5G microservice cores.
limitation_or_critique: Focuses on software architecture; scaling, NF selection and AI-driven orchestration of the resulting microservices are not evaluated.

expected_title: A Survey on Cloud-Based 6G Deployments: Current Solutions, Future Directions and Open Challenges
summary: Large survey of deploying cellular (5G/6G) core and network functions on public clouds and Kubernetes, with a taxonomy over architecture, orchestration, multi-tenancy and economics.
method: Survey with four-dimension taxonomy and analysis of six investigation areas
key_result: Identifies scalability/elasticity, performance and resilience as key open areas and points to AI-driven orchestration and serverless networking as emerging trends for 6G cores.
limitation_or_critique: Unreviewed preprint; breadth over depth, so NF selection/SCP and learning-based scaling receive only summary treatment.

expected_title: AI-Based Resource Management in Beyond 5G Cloud Native Environment
summary: Magazine article proposing a hierarchical closed-loop, AI-based framework for managing resources of cloud-native B5G network functions, aligned with ETSI ZSM, plus a cloud-native simulator.
method: Hierarchical closed-loop ML management framework; cloud-native simulator
data_or_testbed: Custom cloud-native simulator validated against testbed metrics
key_result: Shows the simulator reproduces real testbed behaviour on several metrics, enabling fast evaluation of AI-based CNF management policies.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluation centres on simulator fidelity rather than on concrete NF scaling or selection decisions in a standard 5GC.

expected_title: Autoscaling Packet Core Network Functions with Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Applies a dueling double deep Q-network to proactively scale cloud resources of packet-core NFs, comparing it with threshold-based autoscaling on a Magma core testbed.
method: Deep RL (D3QN) with reward combining resource usage and workload
key_result: DRL scaling cut dropped sessions by up to two orders of magnitude versus threshold scaling while keeping resource usage within bounds.
limitation_or_critique: Single-NF scaling on a Magma (4G/5G hybrid) core; no coordination with NRF/SCP-based selection or multi-NF dependencies.

expected_title: Safe RL for Core Network autoscaling
summary: Formulates core-network autoscaling as a constrained (safe) RL problem so that exploration avoids unsafe scaling actions during training.
method: Safe reinforcement learning with constraint design and tuning
data_or_testbed: Gym-based simulator and Magma open-source core
key_result: Safe RL agents behaved more safely during exploration than unconstrained RL, improving prospects for real-world deployment.
limitation_or_critique: Short conference paper with limited workloads; safety is defined on resource/QoS constraints only and not tied to 3GPP overload control.

expected_title: Deep learning based resource forecasting for 5G core network scaling in Kubernetes environment
summary: Proposes deep-learning forecasting of CNF resource usage to drive proactive scaling of 5GC functions on Kubernetes, with a dataset generated from a cloud-native 5GC testbed.
method: Deep learning time-series forecasting (multi-horizon)
key_result: The selected model gave more accurate long-horizon resource forecasts than a prior deep-learning baseline.
limitation_or_critique: Forecasting is evaluated in isolation; the closed-loop scaling decisions and their effect on control-plane KPIs are not fully demonstrated.

expected_title: Dynamic Network Slice Scaling Assisted by Attention-Based Prediction in 5G Core Network
summary: Uses an attention-based encoder-decoder for multivariate forecasting of VNF resource usage to scale 5GC network slices proactively, balancing SLA violations against over-provisioning.
method: Attention-based seq2seq forecasting plus proactive scaling policy
key_result: Attention-based prediction improved short- and long-term accuracy and reduced combined SLA-violation and over-provisioning cost versus reactive and baseline proactive scaling.
limitation_or_critique: Scaling is slice/VNF-resource oriented and does not consider SBA-level request routing or NF instance selection after scale-out.

expected_title: Scaling UPF Instances in 5G/6G Core With Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Applies PPO-based deep RL with a threshold-shaped reward to scale containerised UPF instances on Kubernetes according to PDU-session demand, with an SVM guard against unwanted actions.
method: Deep RL (PPO) plus SVM action filter
key_result: DRL saved about 2.7-3.8% of pods on average compared with Kubernetes HPA, and the SVM variant up to 4.5%.
limitation_or_critique: User-plane focus with modest gains and simulation-based evaluation; SMF-driven UPF selection is not jointly optimised.

expected_title: A Reliable AMF Scaling and Load Balancing Framework for 5G Core Networks
summary: Optimisation framework that computes the minimum number of AMF instances from traffic-class distributions and assigns relative capacities for load balancing within an AMF set.
method: Optimisation-based scaling with weighted load balancing
key_result: Resilience level is tunable through the problem formulation and the balancer spreads load evenly across AMF instances.
limitation_or_critique: Demand is assumed known/projected rather than learned online, and evaluation is on a small emulated prototype.

expected_title: Cloud Native 5G: an Efficient Orchestration of Cloud Native 5G System
summary: Proposes an orchestration framework for 5G cloud-native NFs that jointly provisions IT and network resources and automates lifecycle management, validated on an auto-scaling use case.
method: CNF orchestration framework (Kubernetes-based) with auto-scaling
key_result: Reported good deployment and upgrade times, low packet loss and balanced resource allocation in experiments.
limitation_or_critique: Scaling logic is rule-based rather than learned, and comparison baselines are limited.

expected_title: Cognitive Service Architecture for 6G Core Network
summary: Conceptualises a cognitive, bio-inspired (octopus nervous system) service architecture for the 6G core in which distributed intelligence augments the SBA.
method: Architecture proposal with case study
key_result: A case study suggests that distributed cognitive services can improve QoS handling relative to a conventional SBA core.
limitation_or_critique: Visionary design with limited quantitative validation and no mapping to 3GPP NRF/SCP procedures.

expected_title: CoreKube: An Efficient, Autoscaling and Resilient Mobile Core System
summary: Message-focused cloud-native core design with fully stateless workers, a shared state database and a RAN-facing frontend, orchestrated by Kubernetes for autoscaling and self-healing.
method: Stateless worker architecture on Kubernetes
data_or_testbed: 4G/5G standard-compliant implementation on the POWDER platform
key_result: Processed control-plane messages efficiently, scaled dynamically with minimal compute and recovered seamlessly from failures relative to prior cores.
limitation_or_critique: Departs from the per-NF SBA decomposition, so NRF/SCP-based discovery and selection are bypassed; autoscaling relies on standard Kubernetes policies rather than learning.

expected_title: L 2 5GC: A Low Latency 5G Core Network based on High-Performance NFV Platforms
summary: L25GC re-architects free5GC around shared-memory NF communication to remove HTTP/serialisation overhead of the SBI while remaining 3GPP compliant, with improved paging/handover and failure resiliency.
method: Shared-memory high-performance NFV platform for 5GC
key_result: About 50% lower event completion time for several control-plane events and roughly 2x lower data latency during paging and handover versus free5GC.
limitation_or_critique: Current implementation supports a limited number of sessions and trades SBI flexibility for co-located shared-memory communication.

expected_title: Control Plane Performance Benchmarking and Feature Analysis of Popular Open-Source 5G Core Networks: OpenAirInterface, Open5GS, and free5GC
summary: Maps NF operations to 5G procedures and benchmarks the control planes of OAI, Open5GS and free5GC with macro- (procedure time) and micro- (system-call) benchmarking.
method: Macro/micro benchmarking with UE registration traffic generator
data_or_testbed: OAI, Open5GS, free5GC; custom traffic generator; released artefacts
key_result: Macro-level procedure performance correlates with micro-level system-call behaviour, which the authors use to pinpoint architectural improvements per core.
limitation_or_critique: Focuses on registration-type procedures on single deployments; autoscaling and multi-instance NF selection are outside scope.

expected_title: Open-Source 5G Core Platforms: A Low-Cost Solution and Performance Evaluation
summary: Reviews major open-source 5GC platforms and compares their control- and user-plane performance on a COTS 5G SA testbed.
method: Comparative review and experimental evaluation
data_or_testbed: Open5GS, OAI, free5GC on COTS SA testbed
key_result: Open5GS gave the lowest control-plane latencies, OAI the highest data rates and free5GC the lowest resource consumption.
limitation_or_critique: Small-scale single-node testbed; results are sensitive to versions and configuration and do not cover scaling behaviour.

expected_title: Next generation of microservices for the 5G Service-Based Architecture
summary: Evaluates VM-based versus container/serverless deployment of SBA network functions and compares HTTP versions, including HTTP/3 over QUIC, for the service-based interfaces.
method: Experimental comparison of deployment models and HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3
data_or_testbed: Kubernetes microservice testbed with emulated loss/delay
key_result: HTTP/3 brought performance benefits under lossy or delayed links, though connection tracking must be engineered for high request volumes.
limitation_or_critique: Synthetic NF services rather than a full 5GC; 3GPP still mandates HTTP/2 over TCP, limiting immediate applicability.

expected_title: Evaluating 5G Core Service Mesh Encapsulations in Cloud Deployments
summary: Introduces 5G-NECTAR, a framework that wraps 5GC NFs in a custom sidecar-based service mesh with OpenTelemetry/Jaeger tracing to measure overhead in public-cloud deployments across HTTP versions.
method: Service-mesh encapsulation and distributed tracing measurement framework
data_or_testbed: 5G core on AWS with sidecar proxies, OpenTelemetry, Jaeger
key_result: Quantifies the control-plane overhead and cost of service-mesh encapsulation for cloud-hosted 5GC and provides operational lessons for MVNOs.
limitation_or_critique: Measurement study without adaptive or learned routing/selection policies in the mesh.

expected_title: Investigating Inter-NF Dependencies in Cloud-Native 5G Core Networks
summary: Studies how inter-NF dependencies in a Kubernetes-orchestrated free5GC affect resource utilisation during control-plane procedures, using a custom gNB/UE emulator.
method: Experimental characterisation of NF resource coupling
data_or_testbed: free5GC on Kubernetes; custom gNB/UE emulator
key_result: Shows that ignoring inter-NF dependencies leads to inefficient scaling where a single NF can bottleneck the whole core.
limitation_or_critique: Descriptive study on one open-source core; it motivates but does not propose a dependency-aware scaling or selection algorithm.

expected_title: Performance and Viability Analysis of Deploying Cloud-native 5G Autoscaling Platforms
summary: Compares two stateless 5GC autoscaling platforms, CoreKube and free5GC-helm, under high synthetic load on a public cloud.
method: Experimental comparison with PacketRusher load generation
data_or_testbed: CoreKube and free5GC-helm on Hetzner Cloud; PacketRusher
key_result: free5GC-helm autoscaling hit bottlenecks early, mainly because of decisions made in the NRF.
limitation_or_critique: Short workshop-style paper (4 pages) at a new venue; analysis limited to two platforms and reactive autoscaling.

expected_title: TEGRA: A Flexible & Scalable NextGen Mobile Core
summary: Proposes resilient SBA microservice design patterns and state-management strategies and builds TEGRA, an SBA core that aims to be both flexible and high-performance.
method: SBA microservice design patterns, edge-aware state management
data_or_testbed: Comparison with free5GC, Open5GS, Aether, CoreKube
key_result: Reports request processing 20x, 11x and 1.75x faster than free5GC, Open5GS and Aether while matching CoreKube and needing far fewer lines of code for new features.
limitation_or_critique: Unreviewed preprint; gains are against open-source cores and learning-based scaling/selection is not considered.

title: System architecture for the 5G System (5GS)
summary: Stage-2 architecture of the 5GS defining the SBA, NF services, NRF-based discovery, SCP indirect communication models and NF/NF-set selection principles.
method: Standard (Stage 2)
key_result: Defines direct and indirect (SCP, delegated discovery) communication options and NF set/load-based selection inputs that research on NF selection must respect.
limitation_or_critique: Specifies selection inputs and frameworks but leaves selection and load-balancing algorithms to implementation.

title: 5G System; Technical Realization of Service Based Architecture; Stage 3
summary: Stage-3 realisation of the SBA: HTTP/2-based SBI protocol stack, indirect communication via SCP, load and overload control, and error handling.
method: Standard (Stage 3)
key_result: Specifies load-control and overload-control information exchange between NFs and SCP, the hooks for adaptive load balancing.
limitation_or_critique: Overload/load control is signalled but policies are left open, which is where AI-based approaches could plug in.

title: 5G System; Network function repository services; Stage 3
summary: Stage-3 specification of NRF services (NF registration, status subscription, discovery, access token) and NF profile attributes used for selection.
method: Standard (Stage 3)
key_result: Defines NF profile fields such as load, capacity, priority and locality that drive discovery responses and consumer-side selection.
limitation_or_critique: Load information in NF profiles is coarse and update-rate limited, motivating analytics-assisted selection.
